kind: Historical observation-based gridded column dust context
title: Regional dust around Jezero

grid.longitude_convention: east-positive, centres from the original -180 to174 axis

variable.name: cdod610
variable.label: 9.3 μm absorption column dust optical depth, normalized to610 Pa
variable.interpretation: Larger values mean a more opaque dust column in this product; no health or storm category assigned.
variable.not: Not surface dust concentration, visibility in metres, temperature, wind, ionizing dose or a forecast

time.cadence: One diurnally averaged map per sol; overlapping weighted observation windows

representative.long_name: Average Modified Julian Date of observations
representative.comment: The average Modified Julian Date of all observations used to reconstruct a map at a given Time, used as representative MJD of the corresponding map. Because in this dataset we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD maps per sol, the average Modified Julian Date of observations is calculated as the average of all four, each of them calculated as the average of the Modified Julian Date of all respectively used observations. The Julian Date can be obtained by adding 2400000.5 to the Modified Julian date.

cell_date.long_name: Grid point Modified Julian Date anomaly
cell_date.comment: The anomaly of the grid point Modified Julian Date with respect to the average (representative) Modified Julian Date of all observations used to reconstruct a map at a given Time. The anomaly of the grid point MJD is obtained by subtracting the value of the corresponding aveMJD variable from the grid point MJD, which is calculated as the weighted average of the Modified Julian Dates of the observations (as for the CDOD values). The grid point Julian Date can be obtained by adding 2400000.5 and the value of the corresponding aveMJD variable to the grid point MJD anomaly. Because in this dataset at each grid point we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD values per sol, the grid point Modified Julian Date anomaly is calculated as diurnal average as well.

time.gap_policy: NaN cells retained as null. Maps with unavailable representative dates omitted without assigning replacement dates.

producer_attributes.title: Gridded column dust optical depth (CDOD) for MY36 produced using iterative weighted binning (IWB). This dataset includes diurnal averages of four values per sol, which are provided as a separate dataset (version 2.5.1). Observations are from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter/Mars Climate Sounder v5.2 (there is no use of Mars Odyssey/Thermal Emission Imaging System in this version). Values are provided for the CDOD (in absorption at 9.3 micron wavelength) normalized to the reference pressure level of 610 Pa, as well as for the non-normalized CDOD (i.e. the total optical depth down to the local grid point surface -see Appendix B of Montabone et al., 2015, for details).

producer_attributes.comment: About units of dimensionless quantities. In general, we use 1 for the unit of dimensionless quantities following the convention of considering such quantities as quantities of dimension one (International vocabulary of metrology -Basic and general concepts and associated terms (VIM)). Exceptions are the use of the dimensionless units of degrees for angles and Pa/Pa for the CDOD normalized to 610 Pa, which results from the ratio of two quantities having the same units.

value.long_name: IR absorption CDOD normalized to the reference pressure of 610 Pa
value.comment: See Equations 1 and 3 of Montabone et al., 2015. In this dataset we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD values per sol.

uncertainty.long_name: Combined uncertainty of CDOD normalized to the reference pressure of 610 Pa
uncertainty.comment: See Eq. 5 of Montabone et al., 2015 for the calculation of the combined uncertainty of a grid point. Because in this dataset we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD values per sol, the uncertainty provided here is further calculated as combined uncertainty of the four values with weights equal to 1.

window_sols.comment: The minimum time window within which averaged observations provided a valid grid point. Because in this dataset we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD values per sol, the time window of observations is calculated as diurnal average as well.

observation_count.comment: The number of averaged observations that contributed to the corresponding valid grid point. Because in this dataset we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD values per sol, the number of averaged CDOD observations is calculated as diurnal average as well.

reliability.comment: The reliability value of the grid point, calculated as the weighted average of the reliability values of the observations (see Section 2.4 of Montabone et al., 2015). Because in this dataset we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD values per sol, the reliability value is calculated as diurnal average as well.

mjd_anomaly.long_name: Grid point Modified Julian Date anomaly
mjd_anomaly.comment: The anomaly of the grid point Modified Julian Date with respect to the average (representative) Modified Julian Date of all observations used to reconstruct a map at a given Time. The anomaly of the grid point MJD is obtained by subtracting the value of the corresponding aveMJD variable from the grid point MJD, which is calculated as the weighted average of the Modified Julian Dates of the observations (as for the CDOD values). The grid point Julian Date can be obtained by adding 2400000.5 and the value of the corresponding aveMJD variable to the grid point MJD anomaly. Because in this dataset at each grid point we provide the diurnal average of four CDOD values per sol, the grid point Modified Julian Date anomaly is calculated as diurnal average as well.

limitations: Cells are about300–355 km wide near Jezero; the local Marswalk is much smaller.
Values are gridded and diurnally averaged retrieval estimates, not direct point readings.
Overlapping multi-sol observation windows smooth changes; no hourly timing or independent day-to-day samples implied.
History is not a forecast; no plume tracking, safe departure, exposure dose or EVA certification.
MEDA station sol16 is independent and stays fixed to its recorded place/time.
